items.title: fix(control-ui): avoid warm chat reload backtracking (#193217)
items.summary: fix(control-ui): avoid warm chat reload backtracking (#193217) On a warm reload of an active chat, automatic end-follow aimed at estimated heights for the newly appended rows. Once the real measurements replaced those estimates, the transcript scrolled backward. A later tool completion repeated the correction. On Peter's real page this showed up as repeated corrections over roughly 500 ms and a CLS of 0.11 to 0.12. Automatic end-follow now picks its destination from the existing native measurement batch. It waits until the mounted destination rows and their virtual sizes agree, and the competing synchronous warm measurement pass is gone. The measured window covers the full destination viewport, including several appended turns. Warm reader restoration joins that same batch. Real older-history prepends keep the synchronous anchor they need before paint, because deferring that boundary broke continuous native reading. Arrival retires the scroll command through its existing owner. Retargeting keeps an already-issued smooth destination while its measured replacement is prepared, so native motion that is still running is not mistaken for reader input. No store, config, protocol field or cache shape is added. Proof: 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A on a quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge (132 pair deltas in total), Team-scale fixture. - Active-chat backtracking goes from 76 to 0 px in 11/11 pairs. A planned second block confirms it. - History replacement followed by tool completion goes from 144 to 0 px in 11/11. - Both reader variants keep 0 px movement with no missing anchor frames. - RPC counts and payloads are unchanged in every pair. - The native regression e2e fails on the pre-fix code and passes on this head. The lead accepted a recorded cost exception: +34 ms total blocking, +21 ms forced style/layout in the 700-1300 ms replacement window, and +7 ms final rows. That cost delays no visible content (same precedent as #190925). Exact-head CI is green. Chat boot JS is +661 B against its base and stays inside the unchanged 1,289,030 B cap. No cap or baseline changed. The full UI suite's three reds reproduce identically on main. The test-lines checker now lets an exact allocation reconcile the base's existing overage without creating slack. The bound is own growth plus inherited debt, floored at zero, with real-Git regression cases. This PR's allocation is 278 lines: 273 regression-test lines plus 5 lines of lead-approved inherited debt.
